pattern.short_summary: The user builds up a standing set of rules, principles, or preferences that is stored outside any single generation and consulted on every subsequent run.
pattern.definition: The user builds up a standing set of rules, principles, or preferences that is stored outside any single generation and consulted on every subsequent run. Entries are authored by the user, usually in natural language, and the set is displayed as an inspectable, editable list. The set governs generation as a persistent policy rather than as a one-off instruction.
pattern.structural_signature: A named collection with add / edit / remove / reorder operations, persisted across generations and rendered as a list. Each entry originates from a user act (typed preference, feedback on an output converted into a rule, an imported written protocol) and is compiled into something the generator consults — a prompt fragment, an executable predicate, a decoding constraint, an ordering. Priority among entries may be expressed by position in the list rather than by numeric weight.

dimension.category_description: Visible rules or boundaries that restrict generation, protect artifact regions, preserve privacy, or reserve part of the task for the user.
dimension.classification_boundary: The constraint must be expressed through the interface or directly shape an observable interaction; invisible policies are excluded.
